memory_candidates.content: Claude Code skill frontmatter `allowed-tools:` has no in-repo precedent for multi-pattern-per-line tool scoping (e.g. `Bash(cmd1:*), Bash(cmd2:*), Read(path/*)`). Only single-pattern precedent found repo-wide: `skill-git-workflow: allowed-tools: Bash(git:*)`. settings.json's `permissions.allow` array is a separate mechanism (JSON list) and not evidence for frontmatter multi-pattern support. When a plan calls for multi-pattern frontmatter scoping and no sandboxed harness exists to verify enforcement, prefer the documented prose-forbid-list fallback (unscoped tool name + an explicit prose 'Forbidden Operations' section) over shipping unverified syntax.

When a skill's state-machine prose mixes multiple '#### State: X' handlers for the same state (e.g. a primary handler plus an 'optional' parallel variant), verification scripts/graders that grep for 'exactly one handler' will fail unless the alternate path's heading is removed entirely (not just its body/code-block). Disabling a feature documented as its own heading should demote it to a plain paragraph without a heading, not just mark the heading 'DISABLED'.

wrap-up.md's orchestrator handoff schema (H9 contract) canonical sorry_inventory entry schema is {file, line, statement, strategic, assumption, why_deferred, follow_up_task} at the array level, with a top-level `skeleton` boolean on the handoff itself. `follow_up_task` (singular, per sorry_inventory entry) is the actually-shipped field for routing skeleton-exhaustion follow-ups — NOT a top-level `.follow_up_tasks` (plural) field, which some skills (e.g. skill-implementer-hard Stage 3b) optimistically read but which wrap-up.md never populates. Any orchestrator logic deriving follow-up tasks from a skeleton handoff must read `[.sorry_inventory[]?.follow_up_task | select(. != null)] | unique`.
